Use this page to understand validation files, execution order and reference matching.

## Organize the validation files

| File                               | Purpose                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `validation.yaml`                  | Execution order                |
| `structure-validation.yaml`        | Sheet order and dimensions     |
| `generated-validation.yaml`        | Generated field checks         |
| `business-validation.yaml`         | Custom business checks         |

The process file lists the rules to run against the supplied form model:

```yaml
rulesets:
  structure: structure-validation.yaml
  content:
  - generated-validation.yaml
  - business-validation.yaml
```

Validation runs in this order:

1. Check the form structure. Any structural error or unfinished check blocks content validation.
2. Run generated field checks.
3. Run business checks, even when earlier content checks found problems.

### Reuse plans and references

Validation plans and prepared reference snapshots can be reused across submissions with the same rules and references.

Missing or malformed references affect execution only when an eligible reference check needs them.

Reference checks use the shared lookup mechanism from `form.references`, regardless of the catalogue name.

## Read a rule

A rule identifies a field, a check and its parameter:

```yaml
rules:
  field/Observations.count/mandatory: true
  field/Observations.count/type: integer
  field/Observations.count/minimum: 0
  field/Observations.unit/enum: [cm, m]
```

For example, `Observations.count` must be present, contain an integer and be at least zero.

Rules report errors by default. To report a warning instead, supply `value` and `severity` explicitly:

```yaml
rules:
  field/Observations.station/reference: {value: {id: code_lists/stations/code, matching: exact}, severity: warning}
```

Change generated rules by editing the form model and regenerating them.

Enum case matching is configured directly on the validation rule; regeneration preserves this option.

```yaml
rules:
  field/Observations.unit/enum: {value: [cm, m], ignore_case: false}
```

Omitting `ignore_case` defaults to `true`. This changes comparison only; submitted and declared values stay unchanged.

A field's `reference` binding generates a reference check with a catalogue/table/lookup ID and matching mode.

Each submitted value must match exactly one reference row. Supply aliases to accept alternative spellings.

For custom R callbacks, follow [Authoring validation rules](rules-authoring.html).

## Primary keys

A table's `primary_key` declaration generates two explicit content rules:

```yaml
rules:
  sheet/Observations/primary_key_present: [station, observation_id]
  sheet/Observations/primary_key_unique: [station, observation_id]
```

Both report errors. `severity: error` can also be written explicitly with the `value` mapping syntax.

Presence reports each row with a missing component, using the configured missing-value policy.

Uniqueness reports every row sharing a complete, correctly typed key, including the first occurrence.

Incomplete keys are handled by presence; incorrectly typed components remain the responsibility of type checks.

Checks run after value preparation. Findings retain physical Excel rows and named key values.

The engine caches key fields and compares tuples without joining values with separators.

Regenerate rules after changing a key. The loader rejects generated rules that no longer match the model.

## Optional composite keys and row completeness

Table sheets can declare these independent constraints:

```yaml
unique_key: [station, category]
at_least_one: {fields: [category, count], severity: warning}
```

`unique_key` checks uniqueness only when every component is supplied and correctly typed.
It does not make its fields mandatory. Every occurrence of a duplicate complete key is reported as an error.
A sheet may declare both a primary key and a unique key; they are checked independently.
Parent relationships continue to reference a parent's primary key.

`at_least_one` requires a supplied value in at least one selected field on each populated row.
A row is populated when any declared field has a supplied value after preparation.
Entirely empty rows are skipped. Zero and false count as supplied values.
Both constraints use the validation engine's configured missing-value policy.

Both field lists must be nonempty, contain no duplicates, and name declared fields in the same table.
`at_least_one` accepts `error`, `warning`, or `info`; omitted severity defaults to `error`.

Generated rule IDs are `sheet/<sheet>/unique_key` and `sheet/<sheet>/at_least_one`.
Their values are the ordered field lists. The latter preserves the declared severity.
Regenerate validation files after changing either declaration.

## Sequences

A field's `sequence` declaration generates an explicit content rule:

```yaml
rules:
  field/Observations.observation_id/sequence: {value: {start: 1, group_by: [station]}}
```

Numbering follows worksheet row order within each group, even when groups are interleaved.

The first row expects 1, the second 2, and so on. String IDs may have leading zeroes.

Each finding gives the expected number and cell location. Primary-key rules handle uniqueness separately.

## Interpret the result

| Result             | Meaning                                  |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `result$findings`  | Problems found and their cell locations   |
| `result$execution` | Checks completed, unfinished or failed    |
| `result$complete`  | Whether all required validation completed |
| `result$valid`     | Whether the submission passed validation |

Accept a submission only when `result$complete` and `isTRUE(result$valid)` are both true.

## Accept alternate reference codes

Supply aliases when more than one spelling is explicitly accepted for a code:

```r
# Prepare reference values.
reference_values <- list("code_lists/units/code" = list(values = c("cm", "kg"), aliases = c(CM = "cm")))
```

Reference rules ignore case by default, including aliases. Submitted and reference values remain unchanged.

```yaml
rules:
  field/Observations.unit/reference: {value: {id: code_lists/units/code, matching: exact}, ignore_case: false}
```

Use strict matching if case variants identify different canonical codes. Regeneration preserves this option.

Each alias must point to an existing reference value. A missing reference list leaves the check unfinished.

## Match reference names

Reference rules ignore case by default. Use `ignore_case: false` for case-sensitive comparison:

```yaml
rules:
  field/Observations.observer/reference:
    value: {id: registries/contacts/name, matching: name}
    ignore_case: false
```

The option also controls case in aliases and name fallback. Multiple matching reference rows remain ambiguous.

Enable name matching when accents or word order may differ:

```r
# Prepare reference index.
reference_index <- form.references::reference_index(c("MARTIN Emile", "Jane Smith"), matching = "name",
  aliases = c("J. Smith" = "Jane Smith"))
# Display the number of matching rows for each submitted value.
lengths(form.references::reference_match_rows(reference_index, c("Emile Martin", "J. Smith", "Unknown")))
# 1 1 0
```

The first two values each match one reference entry; `Unknown` matches none.

A successful match must identify exactly one entry. Multiple matches remain ambiguous.
